title: The nuns of Helfta
hookLine: Gertrude and Mechthild, whose visions of Christ's heart prepared the Sacred Heart devotion

lines: NEAR ENOUGH TO HEAR HIS HEART.
cards: At the Last Supper, the Gospel of John gives one small, close detail. In the Douay-Rheims: "Now there was leaning on Jesus' bosom one of his disciples, whom Jesus loved."
One disciple, head against the chest of Christ, near enough to hear his heart.
Centuries later, in a convent in Saxony called Helfta, women sang that Gospel in choir and read it in their books, and some of them prayed their way into that very spot.

teach.b: Start with two women in one house. Mechthild of Hackeborn led the singing in the convent choir. Gertrude, remembered as Gertrude the Great, came to Helfta as a child and grew into a scholar of scripture.
Both received visions, and their sisters helped write them down: Gertrude's in a book called the Herald of Divine Love, Mechthild's in the Book of Special Grace. Next, the heartbeat.
In the Herald, on the feast of Saint John, Gertrude sees herself resting beside John at the Lord's breast, and she hears his heart beating.
So she asks John a bold question: you heard this too, so why did you write nothing about it?
In her account, John answers that the sweetness of those heartbeats was kept for later times, when the world had grown cold and would need warming. Then, the wound.
John's Gospel says that at the cross, "one of the soldiers with a spear opened his side, and immediately there came out blood and water."

teach.h: THE OPENED SIDE BECOMES A DOOR.
teach.b: For the women of Helfta, that opened side became a door: a way into the heart of Christ, a place to rest, to be known, to pray.
Later Catholic devotion to the Sacred Heart grew around other visionaries, and some histories of it begin here, with these singing, reading women and a heart they heard beating.

how: Catholics keep the Solemnity of the Most Sacred Heart of Jesus each year, and some honor Saint Gertrude on her feast in November; images of the Sacred Heart hang in homes and churches, and some families enthrone one in the house.

games.why: she asks why his Gospel is silent about them. in her account, he says that sweetness was kept for later times, when the world would need warming.

practice: Sit comfortably and lay one hand flat on your chest until you feel your heartbeat, or just the rise and fall of breath under your palm.

If you pray, let Jesus's words in Matthew ride on the beat: learn of me, because I am meek, and humble of heart. If you don't, simply listen to the heart that has kept beating for you all your life without being asked.

wordCard.voice: Helfta. The convent in Saxony where Gertrude and Mechthild wrote of visions that drew them close to the heart of Christ. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: the heart of christ. The week ran from a quiet ox and a road through creatures to roses in an apron, a king at table, stones for grandchildren, light in glass, and a heartbeat. Rest well, and see you tomorrow.
